source_review.notes: Checked current official Amazon S3 performance guidance; current Google Cloud Storage request, quota, and bandwidth guidance; current Azure Storage scale targets; current Amazon EBS I/O and instance-limit guidance; current Apache Hadoop HDFS architecture and NameNode locking documentation; current Apache Iceberg file/streaming maintenance guidance; and current Apache Parquet sizing guidance. All thirteen final references returned HTTP 200. Service-specific targets, errors, accounting, and ramp behavior are attributed.

evidence: Reviewed useful bytes, request/operation count, deadline, mean bytes/request, bandwidth/request/IOPS ceilings, useful goodput, request rate/latency/in-flight work, amplification, and utilization notation.
Checked matching read/write direction, scope, time window, operation-size accounting, decimal/binary units, and logical-versus-physical boundaries.
Checked that application requests, device operations, object count, metadata calls, physical/billed bytes, cache hits, and committed goodput remain distinct.
notation_and_syntax.notes: The minimum-of-ceilings formula is explicitly simplified and provider limits/defaults are versioned inputs rather than universal constants.

evidence: Executed the Python 3 fixture and reproduced 1,310,720 objects, 364.1 requests/s, and 2.844 GiB/s for a 10-TiB one-hour scan using 8-MiB objects.
Recomputed the request-derived ceiling as 1,000 times 8 MiB = 7.8125 GiB/s, leaving the independent 6.000-GiB/s bandwidth ceiling binding.
Recomputed the 80% safe limit as 4.800 GiB/s and Little's-Law average concurrency as 364.1/s times 0.050 s = about 18.2.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Safe average fit excludes request/size distributions, bursts, retries, metadata, client/network constraints, tail latency, and downstream service.

evidence: Verified useful goodput is bounded by both byte bandwidth and request rate times useful bytes/request before other service centers.
Verified the ideal completion lower bound is the maximum of byte-demand/bandwidth and request-count/request-capacity.
Verified Little's Law relates stable average in-flight work, rate, and mean latency but does not establish safe concurrency under bursts or tail constraints.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Mixed object sizes and operation classes require cohort-specific bounds; raising a nonbinding limit cannot change the first binding service center.

evidence: Reviewed empty/tiny/huge objects, mixed/random/sequential I/O, operation splitting/merging, hot/new/sequential key ranges, sudden ramps, and cold/warm cache.
Reviewed metadata/list storms, range boundary/short-read/version errors, multipart ambiguity, throttling/timeouts, corrupt data, retries, speculation, and burst-credit exhaustion.
Reviewed client/network/volume/account caps, node/zone loss, recovery plus foreground/background traffic, and isolation of destructive benchmarks.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Data, metadata, request, IOPS, byte, client, network, and downstream bottlenecks are diagnosed as separate failure surfaces.

evidence: Traced logical bytes through encoding/compression, ranges, replication, retries/speculation, physical transfer/storage, and one-winner committed output.
Checked range-read record coverage, stable object versions, valid decode boundaries, checksums, and full-record emission.
Checked multipart session/part ownership, checksums, preconditions, ambiguous-completion reconciliation, winner publication, and orphan cleanup.
invariant_checking.notes: Retry/backoff, ramping, compaction, caching, and transfer reshaping must preserve idempotency, snapshots, security, retention, and recovery.

evidence: Reviewed the multi-ceiling bound across byte, request, accounted-operation, metadata, client, network, and downstream centers.
Reviewed read-coverage and write-publication arguments for range and multipart operations under truncation, retry, speculation, and ambiguous responses.
Reviewed stable overload control requiring adaptive admission plus bounded jittered retries to reduce offered load below service long enough to drain queues.
proof_review.notes: Documented quotas, high throughput, absence of explicit throttles, or warm-cache performance alone does not prove the end-to-end storage objective.

evidence: Audited throughput, IOPS, request rate, latency, queue depth, goodput, scale target, throttling, small-file amplification, range, multipart, and retry-amplification terminology.
Confirmed object/API request, filesystem metadata RPC, application I/O, device-accounted operation, catalog commit, and physical/billed transfer are not conflated.
Confirmed cache, burst credits, provisioned capacity, achieved service, safe envelope, and sustained versus microburst rates remain distinct.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Object, block, distributed-filesystem, and table-format mechanisms are concrete implementations of the general multi-service-center model.

evidence: Reviewed logical/encoded/physical/billed bytes, request/IOPS/throughput rates, object/I/O/range/part sizes, queues/concurrency, latency, and errors/throttles/retries.
Reviewed cache, listings/manifests/commits, client CPU/memory/network, volume/service/account quotas/credits, compaction/recovery traffic, and cost.
Confirmed segmentation by execution, tenant/resource/object/range, operation/status, client/instance/location, format/codec, size/cache/load cohort, percentile, and window.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: One large sequential run, mean object size, cached scan, request count, IOPS, or byte rate is not mislabeled as complete storage evidence.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed storage service centers, byte/request demand, IOPS/throughput, Little's Law, metadata/data paths, sizing, range/multipart safety, ramping, overload control, client/network limits, cache, shared work, failure, benchmarking, and observability.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed implementable per-resource admission, exponential jittered retries, range and multipart evidence, metadata pruning/compaction, client and provider metrics, cold/sustained tests, recovery capacity, and destructive-test isolation. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from multi-ceiling vocabulary through diagnosis and safe control. Ten examples and five answered exercises cover object/request arithmetic, request-versus-byte limits, concurrency, small files, I/O accounting, client caps, ambiguous completion, overload, bound selection, metadata diagnosis, and experiments.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external S3/GCS/Azure/EBS/HDFS/Iceberg/Parquet maintainer, storage/filesystem/cloud/runtime/network/platform/SRE/security/economics specialist, production operator, provider representative, downstream consumer, affected user, governance or accessibility specialist, or certification review is claimed.
